newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia bank system '96 pretax profit up 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia bank system '96 pretax profit up 27 pct.

text.p: The preliminary pretax profit for Malaysia's banking system grew 27 percent to 8.7 billion ringgit last year, Bank Negara said on Friday in its annual report for 1996.

Total assets of the Malaysian financial system increased by 22.4 percent in 1996 to 915 billion ringgit against growth of 19.5 percent in 1995 to 747.6 billion ringgit, the central bank's report said.

"The increase in resources (was) recorded mainly by the banking system, with resources rising sharply by 113.9 billion ringgit or 22.1 percent, compared with an increase of 74 billion ringgit or 16.7 percent in 1995," the report said.
The commercial banks were the main contributors, adding 6.2 billion ringgit to the total industry's pretax profit.
Bank Negara said the growth in pretax gains was lower than 1995's 32 percent, but that this was due to higher general provisioning for bad debts made by financial institutions.
Bad debt provisions jumped 61.1 percent year-on-year to 2.39 billion ringgit in 1996, after falling by 19.7 percent in 1995 to 1.48 billion.
Bank Negara said the higher provisioning was due to both the expansion in loan base and the high provisioning policy maintained by an increasing number of banks.
The move will help them "build up cushions to render them less susceptible to any adverse downturn in the economy", the report said.
The percentage of general provision to total gross loans was 1.9 percent as at end-1996, up from 1.6 percent at end-1995.
A Bank Negara official said the central bank does not have an upper limit for general provisioning for an individual bank, though it has a lower target of one percent to total gross loans.
